chapter: Pontiac childhood, family and piano training
title: The player piano and teacher Pauline McCann
summary: The family player piano and rolls fascinated him; his first teacher, Pauline McCann, a black concert pianist and singer.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Let’s talk a little bit about that piano in your living room. There was a piano in your living room right?

Oh, definitely. There was a piano. In fact, it was a player piano. It was always a player piano, until I bought one of my own. All of the pianos that we owned were player pianos. Of course, there was the inevitable role, Which I used to listen to all the time, and I was amazed because I didn't understand it. I would see the keys moving you know, and I could hear the sounds. This intrigued me. That might have had something to do with the fact that I gravitated towards jazz, although, I did not

start out to be a jazz pianist. My mother gave me lessons and I took lessons for about 12 years, but I didn't know anything about jazz. I learned everything about jazz from listen to the records and listening to the player piano roles. Also, I had a teacher was an excellent pianist, and also an excellent singer by the way, Pauline McCann. She was a fantastic pianist, and she was excellent. She was a concert pianist. She had a voice. She later came to New York and had a part in the Carmen Jones, which gives you an idea of how good she was as a singer. But anyway, she was my teacher for the time that I was in Pontiac.
I want to clarify this: she’s black?
Would you have thought of, or would your family have thought of any piano teacher? Was it sort of…

Well, I think they thought of her, primarily, well, not only because she was available, but also that was her profession. But, she was such a fine artist. Where you find anybody better? There was nobody better than that in Pontiac!
